quizzes.description: Master the fundamentals of HTML, CSS, and web architecture.

questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.

questions.question: Which CSS property is used to change the text color of an element?
questions.explanation: The 'color' property specifies the color of text inside an element.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <head> tag in HTML?
options: To display the main title on the page
To contain metadata and links to scripts/stylesheets
To define the footer of the document
questions.correctAnswer: To contain metadata and links to scripts/stylesheets
questions.explanation: The <head> element is a container for metadata and is placed between the <html> tag and the <body> tag.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a valid CSS display property value?
questions.explanation: 'spacing' is not a value for the display property. Common values include block, inline, flex, and grid.

questions.question: What does the 'box-sizing: border-box' property do?
options: Adds a border to every element
Includes padding and border in the element's total width and height
Forces all elements to be square
Excludes padding from the width calculation
questions.correctAnswer: Includes padding and border in the element's total width and height
questions.explanation: Border-box tells the browser to account for any border and padding in the values you specify for an element's width and height.

quizzes.description: Deep dive into closures, prototypes, and asynchronous patterns.

questions.question: What is a 'closure' in JavaScript?
options: A way to close the browser tab
A function combined with its lexical environment
A method to terminate a loop
questions.correctAnswer: A function combined with its lexical environment
questions.explanation: A closure gives you access to an outer function's scope from an inner function.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to handle asynchronous operations in a synchronous-looking way?
questions.explanation: Async/await allows you to write promise-based code as if it were synchronous, but without blocking the main thread.

questions.question: What is the output of 'console.log(typeof NaN)'?
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, NaN (Not-a-Number) is actually a numeric data type.

questions.question: What is the 'Event Loop'?
options: A loop that listens for mouse clicks only
A mechanism that handles asynchronous callbacks in JS
questions.correctAnswer: A mechanism that handles asynchronous callbacks in JS
questions.explanation: The Event Loop monitors the Call Stack and the Callback Queue to execute code asynchronously.

questions.question: What does the 'bind' method do?
options: Creates a new function with a specific 'this' context
questions.correctAnswer: Creates a new function with a specific 'this' context
questions.explanation: The bind() method creates a new function that, when called, has its 'this' keyword set to the provided value.
